security_audit.summary: All 45 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown syntax, fixed documentation links, expected Lark CLI examples, and multilingual text entropy. However, document creation templates place generated content inside shell-quoted arguments, creating a command injection risk when content is inserted without robust escaping.

remediation.issue: Generated document content is represented inside ANSI-C shell-quoted command arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Pass content through a non-shell argument API, standard input, or a safely created file. Do not interpolate meeting-derived text into a shell command.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Shell Interpolation of Generated Document Content
semantic_findings.description: The document commands place generated content and a document locator inside shell-quoted arguments. Unescaped apostrophes or shell syntax can break quoting and execute unintended commands.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples directly use ANSI-C quoted shell strings for variable generated content. Exploitation depends on literal substitution without robust escaping, but the unsafe pattern is explicit.

content.user_title: Summarize Lark Meetings into Clear Reports
content.value_statement: Reviewing many meeting records takes time and can hide important details. This skill gathers Lark meeting notes and creates a structured daily or weekly report.
actual_capabilities: Interprets common date ranges and defaults to the previous seven days.
Searches Lark meetings in supported date windows and follows pagination.
Retrieves meeting details, note identifiers, document tokens, and available links.
Distinguishes normal and unified notes when handling transcript access.
Creates structured daily overviews or multi-day meeting reports.
Can create or append a Lark document when the user requests it.
limitations: Requires `lark-cli`, a user identity, and prior authorization for the required Lark domains.
Depends on related Lark skills and reference files located beside this skill.
Search windows cannot exceed one month, and several operations require batching.
Unified notes do not provide a separate shareable transcript document link.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Weekly Team Review
use_cases.description: Collect the past week of meetings and organize topics, note links, and transcript availability.

use_cases.title: Track Project Discussions
use_cases.description: Review meetings from a project period and identify which sessions have usable notes.

use_cases.title: Create a Daily Meeting Brief
use_cases.description: Produce a concise overview of today's meetings with available notes and document links.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Today
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize my Lark meetings from today. List each meeting time, topic, note link, and transcript availability.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a simple daily meeting overview.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Weekly Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a meeting report for the past seven days. Include totals, meeting details, note links, and missing-note labels.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Custom Period
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Lark meetings from <start date> through <end date>. Group them by day and distinguish normal, unified, and missing notes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Analyze a specific project or reporting period.

prompt_templates.title: Publish an Advanced Summary
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a weekly meeting report for <date range>. Include complete pagination and transcript routing. Append the final report to <Lark document>.
prompt_templates.scenario: Run the full workflow and publish the result.

output_examples.input: Create a meeting report for the past seven days.
output: Weekly Meeting Report: 12 meetings across five days.

output_examples.input: Append this month's meeting summary to my team document.
output_examples.output: The monthly meeting summary was organized by day and appended to the requested Lark document. Meetings without notes were clearly labeled.

best_practices: Confirm the intended date range before processing a large meeting history.
Authorize only the Lark domains required for the requested output.
Review sensitive meeting details before publishing the report to a shared document.
anti_patterns: Do not assume every meeting has notes or a separate transcript document.
Do not request more than one month in a single meeting search.
Do not place untrusted meeting content directly inside shell command strings.

faq.question: Which Lark identity type is supported?
faq.answer: The workflow supports only a user identity.

faq.question: Which authorization domains are required?
faq.answer: The VC domain supports meeting queries and notes. The Drive domain is also required to read note documents or create reports.

faq.question: What date range is used by default?
faq.answer: The workflow defaults to the previous seven days when no range is provided.

faq.question: Can it search more than one month?
faq.answer: Yes, but the workflow must divide longer periods into separate searches of no more than one month.

faq.question: How are meetings without notes handled?
faq.answer: The report labels those meetings as having no notes instead of omitting them.

faq.question: Can it create a Lark document?
faq.answer: Yes. Document creation or updates are optional and require the related Lark document skill and Drive authorization.
